//: PROPOSED. Never applied to any account. The API task role: what a running control plane may do.
//scope: Every ARN below is a placeholder of the form ${...}. This document is a shape, not a deployment.

Statement.//: GetObject only, and only under the evidence prefix. Without it, no export or replay can read an artifact. Deliberately excludes DeleteObject: retention deletion is a separate identity, so a compromised API task cannot destroy evidence.
Needed to answer whether an artifact exists without fetching it. Scoped to the one bucket: a task that could list every bucket in the account could enumerate other systems' storage.
SSE-KMS means an object read is also a KMS Decrypt. Without this the bucket policy succeeds and the read fails, which is a confusing failure to debug at 3am.
The database URL and object-store credentials. Named individually rather than by wildcard prefix: a wildcard grows to cover secrets nobody intended as new ones are added with matching names.
The queue is a wake-up signal, not the source of truth. Losing this permission degrades latency; it does not lose work, because the job row is in PostgreSQL.

Explicit Deny, because an explicit Deny cannot be overridden by a later Allow anywhere in the policy chain. Evidence deletion is retention's job, performed by a different identity against a workspace's recorded policy. An API task that could delete an artifact could destroy the record of a run it was in the middle of failing.
The control plane does not call a model. The agent does, under a different role, and only after an ExecutionGrant is validated. Denying it here means a bug in an API route cannot spend money.
